g.text: SEND (us -> KWS) - the row is committed BEFORE the email is requested
no DB default, caller supplies it)"
COMMITTED, on its OWN session, BEFORE the
outbound call. Sending first can put a real
email in front of a real parent with no row
for the webhook to match, and KWS will not
replay a delivery on request, so that attempt
Merely flushing into the caller's unit of work
reintroduces the hole by a longer route: the
very error the ordering exists to survive
The reverse failure (a ``sent`` row for an
email that never went) is cheap and self-heals.
rate limit is **10 requests/hour per unique
parent email**, in Test and production alike
REDIRECT return (parent's browser -> us) - DISPLAY ONLY, writes NOTHING
Why this leg may never write consent state.
The signed message carries no timestamp and no
nonce, so a URL a parent once received replays
forever. A consent record creatable by replaying
an old link would not be a consent record.
This route therefore renders and returns; the
webhook below is what makes it true.
WEBHOOK (KWS -> us) - the ONLY leg that writes consent state
productId matches OR is not yet pinned
The callback does not report WHICH method ran
(ADR-018 D1). Combined with the AgeGraph branch,
which verifies a parent by inheritance from another
KWS-enabled service, we cannot evidence HOW a given
parent was verified. That is why the row stores
``enabled_methods`` as a snapshot taken at SEND time
rather than a live read: the operator's own versioned
configuration is the compliance evidence, and it must
not mutate under a past verification.
Three legs, three trust properties (ADR-018 D1):
creates the ``sent`` row, before the call
Stripe-style t=/v1= over the raw body, bounded skew
Environment partition: every row stores its own ``kws_environment``. KWS reports nothing that
would let it be re-derived later, and the app's guard against production credentials fires only
when ENVIRONMENT == "local", which no deployed tier is. A Test verification is not a valid VPC.
